senses.title: By force of habit
senses.definition: in a way produced by a repeated pattern rather than a fresh decision
senses.definitionCN: 由反复形成的模式促成，而非每次重新决定
senses.example: He habitually checks the locks twice before leaving, even in daylight.
senses.exampleCN: 他在离开前习惯性地检查两遍门锁，即使是在白天。
senses.why: The adverb is the habit adjective plus a manner suffix, so it says that a habit is the reason for the doing.
senses.whyCN: 该副词由「习惯」形容词加表方式的后缀构成，因此说明做事的缘由是习惯。

senses.title: As a settled rule
senses.definition: as a regular rule of behaviour, with few exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 作为几乎无例外的一贯做法
senses.example: She is habitually the first to arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 她一向是第一个到的人。
senses.why: A rule kept across many occasions is the adverb's sense of consistency.
senses.whyCN: 在许多场合都保持的规则，就是该副词「一贯」的意思。

senses.title: Frequently, over and over
senses.definition: often and repeatedly, as a matter of course
senses.definitionCN: 经常而反复，且被视为常态
senses.example: Trucks habitually exceed the weight limit on this bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车经常超载通过这座桥。
senses.why: Frequency grows out of repetition, so the adverb also means often.
senses.whyCN: 频率由反复而来，因此该副词也指「经常」。

senses.title: Without thinking about it
senses.definition: with no deliberate attention at the moment of doing
senses.definitionCN: 在做的一刻并没有刻意留意
senses.example: He habitually reaches for the second cup.
senses.exampleCN: 他下意识地又伸手去拿第二个杯子。
senses.why: A habit runs itself, so the adverb can mark an act done without a fresh thought.
senses.whyCN: 习惯自行运转，因此该副词可标出未加新思考的动作。

senses.title: According to institutional practice
senses.definition: following the accepted course of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 按照机构认可的程序
senses.example: The clerk habitually files the forms before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员照例在中午前归档表格。
senses.why: A group's repeated practice turns into a course of action the adverb can describe.
senses.whyCN: 群体反复的做法会变成一条可被该副词描述的行动路线。

senses.title: From dependence
senses.definition: in a way driven by a compulsion rather than a choice
senses.definitionCN: 由强迫性依赖而非选择驱动
senses.example: The patient habitually used the painkiller for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这名患者多年来习惯性使用这种止痛药。
senses.why: Compulsion is habit with the grip tightened, and the adverb follows it.
senses.whyCN: 成瘾是「抓得更紧」的习惯，该副词也随之延伸。

senses.title: As a described pattern in law or reports
senses.titleCN: 惯常地（法律与报告用语）
senses.definition: in formal description, in a way that repeats as a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在正式描述中，以反复成模式的方式
senses.example: The report notes that the firm habitually underreports emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出该企业惯常少报排放量。
senses.why: Formal writing uses the adverb to state a pattern without judging each instance.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作使用该副词陈述模式，而不逐次评判。

senses.title: As part of a daily rhythm
senses.definition: at the same points in a daily or seasonal cycle
senses.definitionCN: 在每日或季节循环的同一时点
senses.example: The herd habitually moves to the river at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 兽群照例在黄昏走向河边。
senses.why: A rhythm kept by repetition is another face of habit, applied to daily timing.
senses.whyCN: 由重复维持的节律是习惯的另一面，用于日常时间安排。

intro.en: Habitually is habitual plus the native manner suffix -ly; habitual comes from Latin habitualis, from habitus 'condition', from habere 'to hold'.
intro.cn: 本词由 habitual 加英语本族方式后缀构成；habitual 来自拉丁语 habitualis，出自 habitus「状态」，词根为 habere「持有」。

items.en: Habere 'to have, hold' supplied the root for words about a held condition.
items.cn: habere「拥有、持有」为表「被持有的状态」的词提供词根。

items.en: Habitus named a settled condition or bearing, and gave English the noun habit.
items.cn: habitus 指稳定的状态或举止，并给英语提供了名词「习惯」。

items.en: Habitualis added an adjective suffix meaning 'of the kind of', describing what belongs to such a condition.
items.cn: 加上表「属于该类」的形容词后缀后，描述属于这种状态的东西。

items.en: English formed the adjective from the noun and then added the native manner suffix, recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语由名词构成形容词，再加本族方式后缀构成副词，最早见于十六世纪。

items.en: Reports, law and zoology later used the adverb for patterns that repeat without a person deciding each time.
items.cn: 报告、法律与动物学后来用该副词指不必每次由人决定的反复模式。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Indo-European base behind habere is generally considered to be a reconstruction; the first adverb citation is not exact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：habere 背后的印欧词基一般认为是重构形式；该副词最早书证年代并不精确。

note.en: Group one holds close forms from the same holding root; group two holds adverbs for what happens again and again.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「持有」词根的形近形式；第二组是表示反复发生的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a repeated pattern; it modifies a noun rather than a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 描述反复模式的形容词，修饰名词而非动词。

entries.definition: The noun naming the pattern itself, with neither adjective nor adverb ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指模式本身的名词，不带形容词或副词后缀。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to accustom, formed with a suffix meaning 'make'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「使习惯」的动词，由表「使成为」的后缀构成。

entries.definition: From the same root through a dwelling verb; it names where something lives.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词经表居住的动词而来，指某物生活之处。

entries.definition: In most cases, said of frequency without the idea of a formed habit.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下，只说频率，不含「已成习惯」的意思。

entries.definition: As part of a set procedure, stressing the schedule rather than the person's grip.
entries.definitionCN: 作为固定程序的一部分，强调流程而非个人的黏着。

entries.definition: At steady intervals, with attention to timing rather than to compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 按稳定间隔发生，关注时间而非强迫性。

entries.definition: As a usual feature of a person or group, said of what is representative.
entries.definitionCN: 作为人或群体的通常特征，指代表性表现。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adverb is the habit adjective plus the native manner suffix.
normal.cn: 该副词由「习惯」形容词加英语本族方式后缀构成。

normal.en: The family runs habit, habitual, habitually, habituate, habituation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括习惯、惯常的、习惯性地、使习惯、习惯化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: habitually late, habitually absent, habitually silent.
normal.cn: 固定说法：惯常迟到、经常缺席、一贯沉默。

normal.en: The adverb can describe a person, a group, an animal herd or a formal report.
normal.cn: 该副词可描述个人、群体、兽群或正式报告。

normal.en: Its force is weaker than deliberately and stronger than occasionally.
normal.cn: 它的力度弱于「故意地」，强于「偶尔」。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pushed under the table before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 想象还没人开口，椅子已被推回桌下。

abstract.en: Picture a hand checking a pocket that has been empty all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手去摸一个空了一整天的口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a herd turning toward the river before the sun has moved.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳还没移动，兽群已转向河边。

examples.en: He is habitually late for the morning briefing.
examples.cn: 他早上的例会惯常迟到。

examples.en: The staff habitually wipe the benches before opening.
examples.cn: 员工习惯性地在开门前擦净长椅。

examples.en: Such firms habitually underreport their waste.
examples.cn: 这类企业惯常少报废弃量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「惯常的」加表方式的副词后缀——以属于习惯的方式去做，就是习惯性地、经常地。

root: 英语 habitual 加本族方式副词后缀；habitual 出自拉丁 habitualis，词根为 habere「拥有、持有」，由「被保持的状态」引申为反复成习；更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one manner: a habit explains the act, then the act becomes a rule, a frequency, a reflex, a procedure, a dependency, a reported pattern and a daily rhythm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种方式展开：习惯解释行为，行为再成为规则、频率、反射、程序、依赖、报告中的模式与日常节律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair pushed back under the table before anyone has asked.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人开口，椅子已被推回桌下。

branches.en: HABIT AS REASON: the plain sense gives habit as the cause, and a cause kept across occasions becomes a rule.
branches.cn: 习惯为因：最普通的义项把习惯当原因，而在多个场合保持的原因就成了规则。

branches.en: REPETITION IN TIME: frequency and daily rhythm are the same repetition seen as count and as clock.
branches.cn: 时间中的反复：频率与日常节律是同一反复在「次数」与「时钟」两个角度上的样子。

branches.en: WITHOUT A FRESH THOUGHT: the doing runs itself, with no decision taken at the moment, which is how habit becomes reflex.
branches.cn: 无需新念头：行为自行运转，当下并不作决定，习惯由此成为反射。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND DEPENDENCE: a procedure is a group's habit, a dependency is habit with the grip tightened.
branches.cn: 机构与依赖：程序是群体的习惯，依赖是抓得更紧的习惯。

branches.en: REPORTED PATTERN: formal writing names a pattern without judging each case.
branches.cn: 被报告的模式：正式写作陈述模式，而不逐案评判。

intro.en: Habitually is an adjective plus a native manner suffix; the adjective is a Latin noun of condition plus an adjective suffix, so the word reads in three parts.
intro.cn: 本词是形容词加英语本族方式后缀；形容词本身是拉丁状态名词加形容词后缀，因此可分三部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere supplies the root through habitus, and the adjective suffix marks belonging to a kind; the manner suffix is native English with no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「持有」的动词经其状态名词提供词根，形容词后缀表「属于某类」；方式后缀是英语本族成分，没有拉丁来源。

items.example: The root carries the idea of something held.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「被持有」的意思。

items.example: The noun named a settled condition.
items.exampleCN: 这一名词指稳定的状态。

items.example: Reading became a habit.
items.exampleCN: 阅读成了习惯。

items.example: The habitual riser beat the alarm.
items.exampleCN: 惯于早起的人比闹钟起得早。

items.example: He habitually checks the locks.
items.exampleCN: 他习惯性地检查门锁。

items.example: Keepers habituate animals to noise.
items.exampleCN: 饲养员让动物习惯噪声。

items.example: Habituation took four weeks.
items.exampleCN: 适应花了四周。

items.example: The habitualness of the gesture went unnoticed.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作的惯常性无人注意。

items.example: The syrup is habit-forming.
items.exampleCN: 这种糖浆容易使人成瘾。

derivatives.zh: 去掉表方式的副词后缀后得到形容词，语义为「惯常的」
由形容词去掉形容词后缀后得到名词，语义为「习惯、习性」
由名词加表「使成为」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使习惯」
由动词加表动作或结果的后缀构成，语义偏移为「习惯化」
由形容词加表性质的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「惯常性」

definition_zh: 惯例；常规；固定程序；日常作息
definition_en: a fixed sequence of things done regularly, often without much fresh thought
core_image: 清晨六点半，同一盏灯亮起，同一只杯子放在桌面同一处，动作像被一条看不见的轨道推着走
scene: 更衣室里，护士们把交接本、药车与签字笔按固定顺序排好，谁也不去想要不要换一种做法。The ward routine had not changed in fourteen years.
sceneCN: 这里本词指每天按固定顺序重复的一整套做法（第 1 个义项：日常固定程序）；句意为这个病房的固定流程十四年没有变过。

pos.zh: 惯例；常规；固定程序（可数与不可数两用）
例行的；常规的；平淡无奇的

derivatives.zh: 由基础词加表方式的后缀构成，语义偏移为「按常规地」
由基础词加表「使…化」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使固定成流程」
由上一动词再加表过程的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「流程化的过程」
由基础词加表「人」的后缀构成，语义偏移为「只按旧例办事的人」

senses.title: The daily order of tasks
senses.definition: the usual order in which the tasks of a day or a job are carried out
senses.definitionCN: 一天或一项工作中按固定顺序进行的那些事
senses.example: Her morning routine begins with a short walk before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她的早晨固定安排是从早饭前的一次短途散步开始的。
senses.why: The word first named a habitual path, so a fixed order of acts keeps the image of walking the same way.
senses.whyCN: 本词最初指常走的那条路，因此「固定顺序」这一义仍保留着沿同一条路行走的意象。

senses.title: Dull repetition
senses.definition: work or activity repeated so often that it feels mechanical and uninteresting
senses.definitionCN: 重复次数太多而显得机械、无趣的工作或活动
senses.example: Filing the same forms every afternoon had become pure routine.
senses.exampleCN: 每天下午整理同样的表格，已经成了纯粹的例行公事。
senses.why: A path walked too many times loses its view, and the word took on the colour of dull repetition.
senses.whyCN: 同一条路走得太多次就没有风景，本词于是带上了乏味重复的色彩。

senses.title: A person's fixed schedule
senses.definition: the fixed times at which a person sleeps, eats, works and rests
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在睡眠、进食、工作与休息上固定的时间安排
senses.example: Night shifts wrecked his routine for months.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班在好几个月里打乱了他的作息。
senses.why: A personal timetable is a path a body learns, so the word names the times a person keeps.
senses.whyCN: 个人时间表是身体学会的一条路径，本词用来指一个人守着的时间。

senses.title: A computer subroutine
senses.definition: a set of coded instructions that a program runs whenever a particular task is needed
senses.definitionCN: 程序中在需要某项任务时被调用的一段编码指令
senses.example: The program calls a short routine to check the disk.
senses.exampleCN: 程序会调用一小段子程序来检查磁盘。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the word because a program follows the same set steps each time it runs.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用本词，是因为程序每次运行都走同一套步骤。

senses.title: A set sequence in performance
senses.definition: a fixed sequence of movements that a performer or dancer repeats in a set order
senses.definitionCN: 表演者或舞者按固定次序重复的一组动作
senses.example: The skater added a new jump to her routine.
senses.exampleCN: 这位滑冰者在她的成套动作里加了一个新跳跃。
senses.why: A rehearsed sequence is a path the body memorises, so the stage kept the same word.
senses.whyCN: 排练好的次序是身体记住的一条路径，舞台因此沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: A standard care procedure
senses.definition: the standard order of checks and care that staff follow for each patient
senses.definitionCN: 医护人员对每位病人依序执行的检查与护理标准步骤
senses.example: The nurse ran through the post-operative routine twice.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把术后常规流程过了两遍。
senses.why: Hospitals reduce risk by fixing the order of steps, and that fixed path became a medical term.
senses.whyCN: 医院靠固定步骤次序来降低风险，这条固定路径便成了医学术语。

senses.title: A fixed training pattern
senses.definition: a set list of exercises done in the same order at every session
senses.definitionCN: 每次训练都按同一顺序完成的一组练习
senses.example: He changed his gym routine after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周之后他换了健身房的训练套路。
senses.why: Training repeats the same movement path until it becomes automatic, exactly what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 训练反复走同一条动作路径直到变成自动反应，正是本词所描述的。

senses.title: A security or inspection sequence
senses.definition: the fixed steps that guards or inspectors follow when checking people, bags or sites
senses.definitionCN: 警卫或检查人员在查验人员、包裹或场所时遵循的固定步骤
senses.example: The guard went through the closing routine alone.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫独自走完了闭馆检查程序。
senses.why: Any place that must not be left unchecked turns the check into a set path, and the word follows.
senses.whyCN: 任何不容漏检的场所都会把查验变成一条固定路径，本词也随之使用。

intro.en: Routine goes back to a Latin phrase for an opened way, which became the French word for a road; French then formed a noun for the habit of taking the same way, and English borrowed it.
intro.cn: 本词可追溯到拉丁语中表「被开出的路」的词组，它先变成法语里表「道路」的词；法语再由它造出表「惯走同一条路」的名词，英语随后借入。

items.en: The Latin phrase meant a way broken open or cleared through, the image of a path made by cutting through obstacles.
items.cn: 这一拉丁词组意为「被开出、被清理出来的路」，意象是一条靠破开障碍而成的通道。

items.en: French shortened the phrase to its word for a road or a chosen way, the ordinary term for any path.
items.cn: 法语把这一词组简化为表「道路、选定路线」的常用词，泛指任何路径。

items.en: French added a noun suffix to the word for a road and produced a noun for the habit of taking the same way, at first a minor word.
items.cn: 法语在「道路」一词后加名词后缀，造出表「惯于走同一条路」的名词，最初只是个不起眼的词。

items.en: English borrowed the French noun in the eighteenth century for a settled course of action, first in court and military language.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入这个法语名词，指固定的行事次序，最早见于宫廷与军事用语。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries it spread to offices, hospitals, gyms, stages and code, always keeping the sense of a repeated path.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，它扩散到办公室、医院、健身房、舞台与代码，始终保留「重复路径」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the Latin phrase is usually reconstructed from a verb meaning to break, and the earliest French and English citations are not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁词组的更深来源通常由表「破开」的动词重构而来，法语与英语的最早书证年代也并无确说。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close and are often taken for one another; group two collects words for habits, plans and repeated action.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近、常被混用的形式；第二组是表示习惯、方案与重复动作的词。

entries.tag: a true relative, but the path itself
entries.definition: A real relative from the same Latin phrase for an opened way: it names the path, while routine names the habit of walking it.
entries.definitionCN: 确为同源，同样出自表「被开出的路」的拉丁词组：它指路径本身，本词则指反复走这条路的习惯。

entries.definition: A separate word for a disorderly retreat or a decisive defeat; despite the shared letters it is not the word for a way.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个词，指溃退或决定性击败；尽管字母相近，它并不是表道路的那个词。

entries.definition: A word of uncertain origin meaning memorisation by mechanical repetition; it sounds like routine but is not related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 来源不确定的词，指靠机械重复来记诵；听起来像本词，却并无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: A word of Scandinavian origin for a deep groove worn by wheels; it is not related to the word for a habitual path.
entries.definitionCN: 源自斯堪的纳维亚语的词，指车轮磨出的深沟，与表「惯常路径」的词并无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: A practice fixed in one person by repeated action; routine can be shared by a whole ward or office.
entries.definitionCN: 因反复而为个人固定的做法；本词则可以是整个病房或办公室共有的。

entries.definition: A regulated plan of diet, exercise or treatment set for a goal, tighter and more purposeful than a routine.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一目标设定的饮食、锻炼或治疗方案，比本词更严格、更有目的。

entries.definition: An official order of steps for a task, often written down; a routine may be unwritten and merely customary.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项任务规定的官方步骤次序，常写成文字；本词可以是没写下来的习惯。

entries.definition: The shape that repeated events make when seen from outside; routine is the doing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 从外部看到的重复事件所构成的形状；本词指做事本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin phrase for an opened way gave French the word for a road, and a road walked daily becomes a routine.
normal.cn: 拉丁语里「被开出的路」这一说法给了法语「道路」一词，而天天走的路就成了惯常做法。

normal.en: The family runs routine, routinely, routinize, routinization, routineer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括惯例、按常规地、使流程化、流程化与墨守成规者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a daily routine, a routine check, break the routine, a workout routine.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：每日流程、例行检查、打破常规、训练套路。

normal.en: The same Latin verb for breaking also gave English abrupt and bankrupt, where something is broken off.
normal.cn: 同一个表「破开」的拉丁动词还给了英语「突然的」与「破产的」，二者都含断裂之意。

normal.en: Routine and route are relatives, but routine is the habit of the path and route is the path.
normal.cn: 本词与「路线」同源，但本词指走这条路的习惯，「路线」指路本身。

abstract.en: Picture a groove worn into stone by feet that always take the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被总走同一线路的脚磨出的石槽。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen where every jar sits in the same place for twenty years.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，每个罐子二十年都放在同一位置。

abstract.en: Picture a stage dancer who can finish the whole sequence while thinking of something else.
abstract.cn: 想象一位舞台舞者能把整套动作做完而心里想着别的事。

examples.en: The office routine slows to a crawl on Friday afternoons.
examples.cn: 周五下午办公室的固定节奏慢得像爬。

examples.en: A change of routine can make a long trip feel new.
examples.cn: 换个固定安排能让长途旅行重新有新鲜感。

examples.en: The machine runs a safety routine before every start.
examples.cn: 这台机器每次启动前都跑一遍安全程序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「被开出的路」与「反复走」合起来看：同一条路走成习惯，就是固定流程。

root: 拉丁语中表「被开出的路」的词组，先简化为法语里表「道路」的词，再加后缀构成表「惯常走法」的名词，英语借入后泛指固定流程；更深来源一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: a path walked again and again until the walking needs no thought.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：一条被反复行走、直到不必再想的路径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn track across a floor, followed by feet that no longer look down.
core.cn: 核心意象：地板上一条被踩出的旧痕，走过的脚已不再低头看它。

branches.en: PERSONAL ORDER: the daily sequence and a person's timetable are the path a body walks without thinking.
branches.cn: 个人次序：日常流程与个人作息都是身体不加思索走出的那条路。

branches.en: WORN SMOOTH: too many repetitions strip the interest out, leaving dull routine.
branches.cn: 磨得光滑：重复太多便磨掉了趣味，只剩乏味的例行公事。

branches.en: CODED PATH: a subroutine repeats the same steps on command, the path turned into instructions.
branches.cn: 编码路径：子程序奉命重复同样的步骤，路径被译成指令。

branches.en: TRAINED BODY: a performance sequence and a workout list are movement paths learned by rehearsal.
branches.cn: 受训的身体：成套动作与训练清单都是靠排练记住的动作路径。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL PATH: wards and guards fix the order of checks so that nothing is skipped.
branches.cn: 机构路径：病房与警卫固定查验次序，以免漏掉任何一步。

intro.en: Routine is a French noun built on a Latin phrase, so its parts can be read from the image of a cleared path.
intro.cn: 本词是法语在拉丁词组基础上构成的名词，因此可以从「被开出的路」这一意象读出它的各部分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer supplies the opened way and the road; the French layer adds the noun of habitual action; English adds only a few native suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层提供「被开出的路」与「道路」，法语层加上表惯常行为的名词，英语只在其后追加少量本族后缀。

items.example: The root appears in English words about breaking: abrupt, bankrupt, interrupt.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在表示断裂的英语词里，如突然的、破产的、打断。

items.example: The noun meant any road, and the phrase joined it to a participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词泛指任何道路，词组把它与一个分词连在一起。

items.meaning: a road or a chosen way
items.example: The courier chose the shortest route north.
items.exampleCN: 信使选了向北最短的路线。

items.structure: route plus a French noun suffix
items.example: The ward routine never varied.
items.exampleCN: 病房的固定流程从不变动。

items.meaning: in the usual order, as a matter of course
items.example: Staff routinely log every visit.
items.exampleCN: 员工按惯例记录每次探视。

items.meaning: to make something a fixed procedure
items.meaningCN: 使流程化；使固定成常规
items.example: Managers routinize what they cannot control.
items.exampleCN: 管理者把管不住的事变成固定流程。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fixed procedure
items.example: Routinization cut errors but froze initiative.
items.exampleCN: 流程化减少了错误，却冻住了主动性。

items.example: A routineer distrusts any new step.
items.exampleCN: 墨守成规者对任何新步骤都不信任。

items.structure: Latin prefix plus the root rupt-
items.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end.
items.exampleCN: 会议突然中断。

latinEntries.meaning: a broken or opened thing; in the phrase for an opened way, the opened part
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被破开之物；在表「被开出的路」的词组中指被开出的部分

由基础词加表「使…化」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使固定成流程」
由上一动词再加表过程的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「流程化的过程」

definition_en: in the usual fixed way, as a regular part of what is done
core_image: 值班表上同一格被反复勾上，勾的人连笔都没有停，心里已经想到了下一件事
scene: 清晨的实验室里，同一批样本被依次编号、离心、记录，操作者没有翻看手册，也没有停顿。The samples were routinely checked for contamination before storage.
sceneCN: 这里本词作副词，表示动作按既定流程反复进行（第 1 个义项：按常规例行地）；句意为样本入库前都会照例做污染检查。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀后得到基础词，语义为「惯例、固定流程」
由基础词加表「使…化」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使成为固定流程」
由上一动词再加表过程的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「流程化」
由基础词加表「人」的后缀构成，语义偏移为「只按旧例办事的人」

senses.title: As a matter of fixed practice
senses.definition: in the fixed order established for a task, without variation
senses.definitionCN: 按某项工作已经定下的固定次序、不作变动地
senses.example: Visitors are routinely asked to sign in at the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 来访者照例会被告知在前台登记。
senses.why: The adverb adds the manner suffix to the noun of habit, so it describes doing something in that habitual way.
senses.whyCN: 副词在表习惯的名词后加了表方式的后缀，因此描述以那种惯常方式做事。

senses.title: Usually, in most cases
senses.definition: in most cases, as the ordinary state of affairs
senses.definitionCN: 在多数情况下，作为寻常状况
senses.example: Such delays are routinely reported in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这类延误在冬季通常都会被报道。
senses.why: What happens by habit happens most of the time, so the adverb slid from manner into frequency.
senses.whyCN: 按习惯发生的事多半时候都会发生，副词于是从方式义滑向频率义。

senses.title: Mechanically, without reflection
senses.definition: by force of habit, with no fresh attention to what is being done
senses.definitionCN: 凭习惯去做，对正在做的事不再重新留意
senses.example: He routinely signed papers he had not read.
senses.exampleCN: 他机械地签下自己没读过的文件。
senses.why: A path walked without looking turns the act into a reflex, and the adverb carries that blankness.
senses.whyCN: 不看路地走会把动作变成反射，副词也带上了这种空白感。

senses.title: Every day, as a daily matter
senses.definition: on each day, as part of the daily order
senses.definitionCN: 每一天都如此，作为每日安排的一部分
senses.example: The tide gauge is routinely read at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 潮位计每天清晨照例被读取。
senses.why: The daily round is the oldest sense of the noun, and the adverb keeps its calendar.
senses.whyCN: 每日循环是名词最古老的义项，副词也保留着这层日历意味。

senses.title: Systematically, as a set procedure
senses.definition: as part of an organised procedure applied to every case
senses.definitionCN: 作为一套有组织的程序，对每一个对象都照此执行
senses.example: Every batch is routinely screened for the same three metals.
senses.exampleCN: 每一批都按程序筛查同样的三种金属。
senses.why: A procedure that covers all cases makes the act systematic, and the adverb marks that coverage.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖所有对象的程序使行为变得系统，副词标记的正是这种覆盖。

senses.title: At regular intervals
senses.definition: at fixed intervals of time rather than once
senses.definitionCN: 按固定的时间间隔进行，而非只做一次
senses.example: The filters are routinely replaced every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 滤芯每季度定期更换。
senses.why: A repeated path has a rhythm, and the adverb can name that rhythm rather than the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 重复的路径带有节拍，副词可以指这种节拍而不只是习惯本身。

senses.title: Commonly, as a general rule
senses.definition: as the general rule that most people or cases follow
senses.definitionCN: 作为多数人或多数情况都遵循的一般规则
senses.example: Economists routinely expect such shocks to fade.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家普遍预期这类冲击会消退。
senses.why: When nearly everyone follows a path, the adverb describes the general rule rather than one person's habit.
senses.whyCN: 当几乎人人都走这条路，副词描述的是通则，而非某人的习惯。

senses.title: By institutional custom
senses.definition: according to the unwritten custom of an organisation rather than a written rule
senses.definitionCN: 依照某个组织不成文的惯例，而非依成文规定
senses.example: The committee routinely meets behind closed doors.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会按惯例闭门开会。
senses.why: Institutions run on paths no one wrote down, and the adverb names that quiet custom.
senses.whyCN: 机构靠没人写下来的路径运转，副词指的就是这种无声惯例。

intro.en: Routinely is the noun routine with the English adverb suffix, and routine itself came from French, which drew it from a Latin phrase for an opened way.
intro.cn: 本词是表「惯例」的名词加英语副词后缀构成；而那个名词来自法语，法语又取自拉丁语中表「被开出的路」的词组。

items.en: The Latin phrase meant a way broken open or cleared through, the image behind the French word for a road.
items.cn: 这一拉丁词组意为「被开出、被清理出来的路」，是法语表「道路」一词背后的意象。

items.en: French kept the road sense and later built a noun for the habit of taking the same way.
items.cn: 法语保留了「道路」义，后来又造出表「惯走同一条路」的名词。

items.en: The French noun named a settled habit of acting, a way of doing things that repeats.
items.cn: 这个法语名词指固定的行事习惯，即反复使用的一种做事方式。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the eighteenth century for an established order of actions.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该名词，指已确立的行事次序。

items.en: English added its native manner suffix to the borrowed noun and produced an adverb that soon also meant usually.
items.cn: 英语在借入的名词后加上本族表方式的后缀，造出副词，很快又带上「通常」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the Latin phrase is usually reconstructed from a verb meaning to break, and the first English adverb citation is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁词组的更深来源通常由表「破开」的动词重构，该副词最早的书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects the noun and its near forms that share letters with the adverb; group two collects adverbs of regularity and frequency.
note.cn: 第一组是与副词共享字母的名词及其近形词；第二组是表示规律与频率的副词。

entries.definition: The base noun and adjective names the fixed order itself, while the adverb names the manner of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 作为基础的名词与形容词指固定次序本身，副词则指做事的方式。

entries.tag: verb, to fix into a procedure
entries.definition: A verb built on the same noun: it means turning an activity into a set procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一名词构成的动词，意为把某项活动变成固定程序。

entries.definition: A noun for someone who follows routine mechanically, with a person suffix rather than an adverb suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 指机械照旧例办事的人，用的是表「人」的后缀而非副词后缀。

entries.definition: A relative from the same Latin phrase, but it is the path, not the way of walking it.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁词组的同源词，但它指路径，不指走它的方式。

entries.definition: At set times or intervals; the emphasis is on the timetable rather than on the absence of thought.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定时间或间隔进行，强调时间表而非不加思索。

entries.definition: Out of a settled personal habit, often with a hint of blame that routine does not always carry.
entries.definitionCN: 出于固定的个人习惯，常带一点责备意味，而本词未必带。

entries.definition: As the usual state of things among many people or cases, with no suggestion of a fixed procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指许多人或许多情况中的寻常状态，并不暗示固定程序。

entries.definition: By an organised method that covers every case, stressing design rather than mere repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 按覆盖每一例的有组织方法，强调设计而非单纯重复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base noun means a habitual path; the adverb suffix turns that into the manner of walking it.
normal.cn: 基础名词指惯常的路径，副词后缀把它转成走这条路的方式。

normal.en: The family runs routine, routinely, routinize, routinization, routineer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括惯例、按常规地、使流程化、流程化与墨守成规者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: routinely checked, routinely collected, routinely ignored, routinely tested.
normal.cn: 固定说法：例行检查、例行采集、通常被忽略、定期检测。

normal.en: The adverb can describe a timetable, a frequency or a blank habit, depending on the sentence.
normal.cn: 这个副词可以指时间表、频率或不带思考的习惯，视句子而定。

normal.en: Compare it with the adjective and the noun: the same root, three different jobs.
normal.cn: 把它与形容词、名词对照：同一个词根，三种不同的功用。

abstract.en: Picture a clipboard where the same line is ticked before the reader reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写字板，读的人还没读到那一行，勾已经先打上了。

abstract.en: Picture a conveyor belt that never pauses for anyone to think.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从不为任何人思考而停下的传送带。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands move while nobody in the room looks up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的指针在走，屋里没人抬头看。

examples.en: Nurses routinely weigh every patient on admission.
examples.cn: 护士照例给每位入院病人称体重。

examples.en: Critics are routinely dismissed as complainers.
examples.cn: 批评者通常被当作抱怨者打发掉。

examples.en: The server is routinely backed up at midnight.
examples.cn: 服务器每天午夜按惯例备份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「惯例」与表方式的后缀合起来看：以惯常的方式去做，就是照例、照常。

root: 由表「惯例」的名词加英语副词后缀构成；那个名词来自法语，更早出自拉丁语「被开出的路」的词组，引申为反复走成的固定做法；更深来源一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: the same path walked again, with the accent on the manner of walking rather than on the path itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：仍是同一条被反复行走的路，只是重心落在走的方式，而非路本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand ticking the same box on a list, moving before the eyes have read the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在清单上勾同一个格子，眼睛还没读到那一行，手已经动了。

branches.en: FIXED MANNER: the core sense describes doing a task in the established order, and the daily sense adds the calendar.
branches.cn: 固定方式：核心义指按既定次序做事，每日义再添上日历。

branches.en: USUAL CASE: what is done by habit becomes what generally happens, until it reads as a general rule.
branches.cn: 通常情形：按习惯做的事变成通常发生的事，最后读作通则。

branches.en: WITHOUT THOUGHT: the same path walked blindly turns the act into a reflex.
branches.cn: 不加思索：同一条路被盲目地走，动作就成了反射。

branches.en: SET PROCEDURE: an organised procedure applied to every case makes the act systematic.
branches.cn: 既定程序：有组织、覆盖每一例的程序使行为系统化。

branches.en: REGULAR RHYTHM AND CUSTOM: fixed intervals and unwritten institutional practice give the adverb its two public senses.
branches.cn: 固定节拍与惯例：固定间隔与不成文的机构做法给出副词的两种公共含义。

intro.en: The adverb is a transparent construction: a borrowed noun of habit plus a native manner suffix, so its parts can be read directly.
intro.cn: 这个副词是透明的构造：一个借入的「习惯」名词加上本族表方式的后缀，因此各部分可以直接读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer supplies the opened way and the road, the French layer the noun of habitual action, and English only supplies the adverb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层提供「被开出的路」与「道路」，法语层提供表惯常行为的名词，英语只提供副词词尾。

items.example: The root appears in English words about breaking: abrupt, bankrupt, interrupt.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在表示断裂的英语词里，如突然的、破产的、打断。

items.example: The noun meant any road, and the phrase joined it to a participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词泛指任何道路，词组把它与一个分词连在一起。

items.meaning: a road or a chosen way
items.example: The courier chose the shortest route north.
items.exampleCN: 信使选了向北最短的路线。

items.structure: route plus a French noun suffix
items.example: The ward routine never varied.
items.exampleCN: 病房的固定流程从不变动。

items.meaning: in the usual order, as a matter of course
items.example: Staff routinely log every visit.
items.exampleCN: 员工按惯例记录每次探视。

items.meaning: to make something a fixed procedure
items.meaningCN: 使流程化；使固定成常规
items.example: Managers routinize what they cannot control.
items.exampleCN: 管理者把管不住的事变成固定流程。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fixed procedure
items.example: Routinization cut errors but froze initiative.
items.exampleCN: 流程化减少了错误，却冻住了主动性。

items.example: A routineer distrusts any new step.
items.exampleCN: 墨守成规者对任何新步骤都不信任。

latinEntries.meaning: a broken or opened thing; the opened part in the phrase for an opened way
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被破开之物；表「被开出的路」的词组中指被开出的部分

definition_en: a leaning or inclination toward a particular kind of behaviour, direction or outcome
core_image: 一枚小球放在微微倾斜的桌面上，手一松，它总是往同一个方向滚
scene: 议事厅里，同一批人每次表决都往同一个方向靠，连反对者也渐渐跟着举手。There was a clear tendency for the committee to side with the older members.
sceneCN: 这里本词指群体在反复选择中表现出的固定偏向（第 1 个义项：一般倾向）；句意为委员会明显倾向于站在年长成员一边。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

senses.title: A general leaning
senses.definition: a general leaning of people or things toward one kind of behaviour or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物总体上偏向某一类行为或结果的态势
senses.example: There is a general tendency for prices to rise before holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 节前价格上涨存在一种普遍倾向。
senses.why: The word began as a stretched direction, and the first sense is that leaning seen in a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 本词最初指被拉伸的方向，第一个义项就是整个群体表现出的这种偏向。

senses.title: A personal habit of mind
senses.definition: a person's habitual inclination to act or feel in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在行为或感受上习惯性的偏向
senses.example: She has a tendency to interrupt when she is nervous.
senses.exampleCN: 她紧张时有打断别人的癖性。
senses.why: A single person also leans one way again and again, and the word names that private tilt.
senses.whyCN: 单个人也会一次次往同一侧倾，本词就指这种私人的偏向。

senses.title: A statistical movement
senses.definition: the direction in which a set of figures moves over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据在一段时间内变动的方向
senses.example: The figures show an upward tendency in household savings.
senses.exampleCN: 数据显示家庭储蓄呈上升趋势。
senses.why: Numbers plotted over time lean visibly, and that lean is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 按时间画出的数据会显出倾斜，本词描述的正是这种倾斜。

senses.title: A current of opinion
senses.definition: a broad drift of opinion or policy in a society at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期社会舆论或政策上广泛出现的走向
senses.example: A reformist tendency gained ground among younger voters.
senses.exampleCN: 改革倾向在年轻选民中占了上风。
senses.why: When many minds lean together, the lean becomes a public current rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的心思同时倾斜，这种倾斜就成了公共潮流而非私人情绪。

senses.title: A physical drift
senses.definition: the direction in which a body or substance naturally moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 物体或物质自然移动或变化的方向
senses.example: Hot air has a tendency to rise above cooler air.
senses.exampleCN: 热空气有升到冷空气之上的趋向。
senses.why: The oldest image is physical: something stretched or pulled toward a point.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是物理性的：某物被拉向某一点。

senses.title: A medical susceptibility
senses.definition: a bodily weakness that makes a person likely to develop a particular illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上的弱点使人容易患上某种疾病
senses.example: The condition runs in families with a tendency to low bone density.
senses.exampleCN: 该病多见于有骨密度偏低易感性的家族。
senses.why: A body leaning toward illness is described with the same word as any other lean.
senses.whyCN: 身体向疾病倾斜，用的仍是与其它倾斜相同的词。

senses.title: A stylistic leaning in art
senses.definition: a recurring preference for certain forms or moods in an artist's work
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家作品中反复出现的对某些形式或情绪的偏好
senses.example: His later novels show a tendency toward long, quiet scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 他后期的小说显出偏爱篇幅长而安静的场景。
senses.why: Style is a repeated lean of the hand, and critics borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 风格是手反复倾斜的结果，评论者便借用这个词来指它。

senses.title: A market drift
senses.definition: the direction in which prices or demand appear to be heading
senses.definitionCN: 价格或需求看起来正在走向的方向
senses.example: Traders watched the tendency of the index for the week.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员盯着这一周指数的走势。
senses.why: Markets are read as leaning one way, so forecasters speak of a tendency rather than a certainty.
senses.whyCN: 市场被看作正在往一侧倾，故预测者说倾向而不说定论。

intro.en: Tendency comes from the Latin verb for stretching or aiming, through a medieval Latin noun for a leaning; it is not related to the word for a trend, which comes from an Old English verb for turning.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，经中世纪拉丁语表「倾斜」的名词进入英语；它与表「走势」的那个词并不同源，后者出自古英语中表「转动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to stretch out, hold out or aim, and the image is a body or a line extended toward a point.
items.cn: 这一拉丁动词意为「伸出、朝向、瞄准」，意象是身体或线条朝某一点展开。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed a noun from the participle of that verb, naming a leaning or an inclination.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用该动词的分词造出名词，指倾斜或倾向。

items.en: English took the noun in the seventeenth century for a leaning of mind, body or fortune.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该名词，指心思、身体或运势上的偏向。

items.en: The word for a trend is not a relative: it comes from an Old English verb meaning to turn or revolve, and only later came to mean a direction.
items.cn: 表「走势」的那个词并非同族：它出自古英语中表「转动、旋转」的动词，后来才引申为方向。

items.en: Source uncertain: the older shape of the Latin verb is generally reconstructed, and the first English citation of the noun is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁动词的更早形态一般为重构，该名词在英语中的最早书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close to this noun; group two collects words for leanings of mind or body.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的形式；第二组是表示心思或身体偏向的词。

entries.definition: A true relative: the verb means to be inclined or to take care of, and the noun adds a suffix of state.
entries.definitionCN: 确为同源：动词表示趋向或照管，名词则加上表状态的后缀。

entries.definition: It means pushing a one-sided view, built on the same leaning root with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 意为推行片面观点，由同一表「倾斜」的词根加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Often treated as a synonym but a different word: it comes from an Old English verb for turning, not from the Latin verb for stretching, so the two are not cognate.
entries.definitionCN: 常被当作同义词，其实是另一个词：它出自古英语表「转动」的动词，而非拉丁语表「伸展」的动词，二者并无同源关系。

entries.definition: It sounds almost the same but comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold, and it names the right to occupy property rather than a leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，却出自拉丁语表「握持」的动词，指占用房产的权利，与偏向无关。

entries.definition: A leaning of mind or body, closer to a settled preference than to a measured direction in figures.
entries.definitionCN: 心思或身体上的倾斜，更接近固定的偏好，而非数据中被测量的方向。

entries.definition: A strong natural tendency to behave in a particular way, usually toward something undesirable.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈而天生的行为偏向，通常指向不受欢迎的事。

entries.definition: A person's habitual temperament, the whole cast of mind rather than one lean.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人习惯的性情，是整个心性而非单一偏向。

entries.definition: A slow general movement or change of opinion, stressing gradual motion rather than a built-in lean.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的整体移动或舆论变化，强调渐进，而非内在的倾斜。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to stretch: a line pulled toward a point, and that is the image of the whole family.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为伸展：一条被拉向某点的线，这就是整个词族的意象。

normal.en: The family runs tendency, tend, tendentious, tendentiously, tendentiousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括倾向、趋向、有偏向的、带有偏向地与偏向性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a tendency to overreact, a downward tendency, a growing tendency.
normal.cn: 固定说法：过度反应的倾向、下降趋势、日益增长的趋势。

normal.en: Keep it apart from the word for a trend: that one came from an old verb for turning, not from stretching.
normal.cn: 要与表「走势」的那个词分开：后者出自表「转动」的古动词，并非出自「伸展」。

normal.en: Statistics speak of a tendency when a line on a chart slants; medicine speaks of one when a body is likely to fall ill.
normal.cn: 统计学说倾向，是指图表上的线出现斜度；医学说倾向，是指身体容易生病。

abstract.en: Picture a metal ball rolling toward the low edge of a tilted table, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗金属球一次次滚向倾斜桌面的低边。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one side of a square without anyone giving an order.
abstract.cn: 想象人群没有接到任何指令，却慢慢移向广场的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that always reaches for the same pen, even when another lies closer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手总去拿同一支笔，哪怕另一支离得更近。

examples.en: Prices show a tendency to fall after the harvest.
examples.cn: 收成之后价格显出下跌的倾向。

examples.en: He has a tendency to talk over people in meetings.
examples.cn: 他在会上有抢别人话头的癖性。

examples.en: The survey found a tendency toward smaller households.
examples.cn: 调查发现家庭规模有变小的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「伸展」记成一条被拉向某处的线：线往哪边斜，就是往哪边倾向。

root: 来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，中世纪拉丁语由其分词构成表「倾斜」的名词，英语借入后指各种偏向；与表「走势」的词不同源，后者出自古英语表「转动」的动词；更深来源一般为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: a line or a body stretched toward one point, so that it leans the same way each time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：一条线或一具身体被拉向某一点，于是每次都往同一侧倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a tilted table, always rolling to the same low corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾斜桌面上的球，总滚向同一个低角。

branches.en: LEANING LINE: the general lean of people and the physical drift of matter share one image of a stretched line.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线：人群的整体偏向与物质的物理趋向共享「被拉长的线」这一意象。

branches.en: PRIVATE LEAN: one person's repeated tilt becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 私人偏向：一个人反复的倾斜成为心理习性。

branches.en: MEASURED SLANT: charts and markets are read as leaning, so the word names a direction in figures.
branches.cn: 可测的斜度：图表与市场都被读作倾斜，本词于是指数据中的方向。

branches.en: PUBLIC CURRENT: many minds leaning together become a drift of opinion.
branches.cn: 公共潮流：许多心思同时倾斜，便成舆论走向。

branches.en: BODY AND ART: a body likely to fall ill and a hand that prefers certain forms both lean in the same old sense.
branches.cn: 身体与艺术：易患病的身体与偏爱某些形式的手，都在同一古老意义上倾斜。

intro.en: The noun is built from a Latin verb and a suffix of state, and English keeps a small family around it, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语动词加表状态的后缀构成，英语周围还保留少量同族词，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb supplies the stretching, the Latin participle supplies the leaning, and English supplies only the closing noun suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词提供「伸展」，拉丁语分词提供「倾斜」，英语只提供收尾的名词后缀。

items.example: The root shows in extend, intend and tension, all about stretching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于延伸、打算、张力等词，都与伸展有关。

items.example: A bowstring is stretched, and so is a plan toward its aim.
items.exampleCN: 弓弦被拉紧，计划也朝目标伸展。

items.example: The participle describes what is already leaning.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词描述已经在倾斜的东西。

items.structure: tendens plus a medieval Latin noun suffix
items.example: The medieval noun turned the act of leaning into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪名词把倾斜这一动作变成一种事物。

items.meaning: a leaning toward a kind of act or outcome
items.example: A tendency can be measured over many cases.
items.exampleCN: 倾向可以在许多个案上被测量出来。

items.example: The report was tendentious from its first line.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告从第一行起就带有偏向。

items.meaning: the quality of pushing a lean
items.example: Readers objected to the tendentiousness of the piece.
items.exampleCN: 读者反对这篇文章的偏向性。

items.structure: Latin prefix plus the root tend-
items.example: They extended the deadline by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把截止期限延长了一周。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch, to extend, to aim

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

definition_zh: 倾向；意愿；倾斜；倾角；斜坡
definition_en: a feeling of wanting to do something, or the angle at which something leans away from the level
core_image: 一根长杆原本立得笔直，有人从顶端轻轻一推，它便朝草地的方向偏过去，停在一个既不直立也不倒下的角度
scene: 院子里两张椅子并排放着，一张在树阴下，一张在阳光下，主人几乎没有停顿就坐进了有太阳的那张。His inclination was to stay in the garden rather than drive to town.
sceneCN: 这里本词指做某事的意愿倾向（第 1 个义项：心里更愿意选择的那一边）；句意为他的意愿是留在花园里，而不是开车进城。

pos.zh: 倾角（天文学、物理学用语）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀，回到同族动词，语义偏移为「使倾斜；倾斜」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，语义偏移为「倾向于……的；倾斜的」
由动词加表「可……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「易受影响而首肯的」
由动词词干加表测量仪器的成分构成，语义偏移为「测斜仪」
由本词加表角度的名词构成，语义偏移为「倾角」

senses.title: A leaning of the mind
senses.definition: a feeling that makes someone want to choose one course rather than another
senses.definitionCN: 使人更愿意选择某一做法而非另一做法的心理状态
senses.example: His inclination was to stay in the garden rather than drive to town.
senses.exampleCN: 他的意愿是留在花园里，而不是开车进城。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bend something; the mind bending toward a choice kept the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是使某物弯曲；心思朝某个选择弯过去，沿用了同一幅画面。

senses.title: The act of leaning
senses.definition: the movement or position of something that leans away from upright
senses.definitionCN: 某物离开直立状态而偏斜的动作或姿态
senses.example: A slow inclination of the mast told the crew the wind had shifted.
senses.exampleCN: 桅杆缓缓倾斜，船员便知道风向变了。
senses.why: The physical sense is the oldest one: a body that is no longer upright has bent away from the vertical.
senses.whyCN: 物理义最古老：一个不再直立的东西，就是从竖直方向弯开了。

senses.title: The size of that lean
senses.definition: the amount by which a line or surface deviates from the horizontal or vertical
senses.definitionCN: 直线或平面偏离水平或竖直的幅度
senses.example: The wall shows an inclination of four degrees from the vertical.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙与竖直方向有约四度的倾斜。
senses.why: Once the leaning was measured, the measurement itself took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜一旦可以测量，这个量本身也用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The tilt of an orbit
senses.definition: the angle between the plane of an orbit and a reference plane
senses.definitionCN: 轨道平面与某一参考平面之间的夹角
senses.example: Pluto's orbital inclination is far larger than that of the inner planets.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星的轨道倾角远大于内行星。
senses.why: Astronomers borrowed the leaning image for a path that is tilted against the sky's flat plane.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家借「倾斜」这一意象，表示相对天空中那个平面而偏斜的路径。

senses.title: The dip of a magnetic needle
senses.definition: the angle at which a compass needle dips toward the earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 指南针指针向下倾入地表的角度
senses.example: Sailors once measured magnetic inclination to guess how far north they were.
senses.exampleCN: 水手曾测量磁倾角来推估自己北行的距离。
senses.why: A needle that dips is a small bar of metal behaving like any leaning object, so the verb's image fits exactly.
senses.whyCN: 指针下倾，就是一小根金属像任何倾斜物体那样偏斜，动词的意象正好合用。

senses.title: A nod of the head
senses.titleCN: 点头或俯身的轻微动作
senses.definition: a slight bending of the head or upper body as a greeting or sign
senses.definitionCN: 作为招呼或示意而微微低头或俯身
senses.example: He answered with the smallest inclination of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他只以极轻微的一点头作答。
senses.why: Bending the body forward is the literal old gesture, and courtesy still borrows it.
senses.whyCN: 身体前弯是字面意义上的古老动作，礼节的表达至今仍在借用它。

senses.title: A natural liking
senses.definition: a natural attraction to a particular activity, subject or kind of person
senses.definitionCN: 对某种活动、学科或某类人天生的亲近感
senses.example: She showed an early inclination for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她早年就显露出对语言的爱好。
senses.why: A liking is the mind leaning without being pushed, so the word names what comes by itself.
senses.whyCN: 爱好是心思自己在弯，不用外力推，因此这个词指自发而来者。

senses.title: A slope in the land
senses.definition: a downward slope of ground, or the degree to which it falls away
senses.definitionCN: 地面向下倾斜的状态或落差程度
senses.example: The orchard sits on a gentle inclination facing south.
senses.exampleCN: 果园坐落在朝南的缓和坡上。
senses.why: Ground that leans is described with the same noun as a mind that leans, and the two images are the same one.
senses.whyCN: 地会倾斜，心也会倾斜，两者用的是同一个名词，本源也是一幅画面。

intro.en: Inclination comes from Latin inclinatio 'a leaning', built on inclinare 'to bend, cause to lean', itself in- plus clinare 'to bend'; the mental sense grew out of the physical one.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语 inclinatio「倾斜」，其动词 inclinare 意为「使弯、使倾」，由表「向内」的前缀加 clinare「弯」构成；心理义是从物理义长出来的。

items.en: Clinare meant 'to bend, to cause to lean', a verb of the physical world rather than of feeling.
items.cn: clinare 意为「弯、使倾」，是物理世界的动词，而非情感的词。

items.en: Latin in- added direction, so inclinare meant 'to bend towards', to lean something in a given direction.
items.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀加在其前，构成「朝某方向弯」的动词，意为把某物往某一侧倾。

items.en: Inclinatio named the state or act of leaning, and could already describe a leaning of the will.
items.cn: 名词形式指倾斜的状态或动作，当时已可用来描述意志的偏向。

items.en: French passed the word to English in the fourteenth century, first as a physical and then as a mental leaning.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把该词传给英语，先指物理倾斜，再指心理倾向。

items.en: Astronomy and geomagnetism took the noun for the tilt of an orbit and the dip of a needle.
items.cn: 天文学与地磁学取用该名词，分别指轨道倾斜与指针下倾。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the first English use is dated to the fourteenth century, while the older base behind clinare is generally considered a reconstruction, not an attested form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语首见书证定于十四世纪，而 clinare 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式，并非已见形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look close to this word and are often confused with it; group two holds words for wanting, leaning and liking that differ in force.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近、常被混用的形式；第二组是表示意愿、倾斜与喜爱的近义词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective; it describes a person or thing that leans, while the noun names the lean itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一动词的过去分词转成的形容词，描述会倾的人或物；本词则是命名倾斜本身的名词。

entries.definition: A fixed compound naming the measured angle; the single noun names the leaning in general.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个词构成的固定组合，指被测出的角度；单个名词则泛指倾斜这件事。

entries.definition: An instrument for measuring a slope; it shares the leaning stem but ends in a device suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 测量坡度的仪器；与本词同出「倾斜」词干，但结尾是表仪器的成分。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone easily persuaded; it describes a person, while the noun describes the leaning itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容容易被说动的形容词；描述的是人，本词描述的是倾斜本身。

entries.definition: A general direction in which something usually moves or behaves, often observed over many cases.
entries.definitionCN: 事物通常朝之发展或表现的方向，多由许多事例观察得出。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a preference or a physical tilt, closer to speech than the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示偏好或物理倾斜的日常词，比这个拉丁名词更口语。

entries.definition: A liking for one thing over another after comparison, sharper than a mere inclination.
entries.definitionCN: 比较之后更喜欢某物，比单纯的倾向更明确。

entries.definition: A slope or a way of presenting something that favours one side, both physical and editorial.
entries.definitionCN: 坡度，也指带偏向的呈现方式，兼有物理与立场两层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real parts: a prefix meaning towards, and a verb meaning to bend.
normal.cn: 两个真实成分：一个表「朝向」的前缀，加一个表「弯」的动词。

normal.en: The family runs incline, inclined, inclination, inclinable, inclinometer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括使倾斜、倾向于、倾向、易被说动的、测斜仪。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: an inclination to do something, follow one's inclination, magnetic inclination.
normal.cn: 固定说法：做某事的倾向、随自己的意愿、磁倾角。

normal.en: Every technical sense measures the same thing: how far a line, a path or a needle has bent from the level.
normal.cn: 每个技术义量的都是同一件事：一条线、一条路径或一根指针偏离水平多少。

normal.en: The mental sense is the physical sense moved inward: the will leans before the body does.
normal.cn: 心理义是物理义向内移的结果：意志先于身体倾过去。

abstract.en: Picture a straight pole pushed at the top until it rests at an angle, neither standing nor fallen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根直杆在顶端被推，直到停在一个斜角上，既没立着也没倒下。

abstract.en: Picture a needle in a glass case dipping its painted end toward the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃盒里的一根指针，带漆的一端朝地面下垂。

abstract.en: Picture a mind that leans toward one door before any argument is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心在还没听到任何理由之前，就已经朝某一扇门偏过去。

examples.en: She has an inclination to argue with every plan.
examples.cn: 她有一种对每个方案都要争辩的倾向。

examples.en: The tower's inclination has been measured for a century.
examples.cn: 这座塔的倾斜已被测量了一个世纪。

examples.en: Follow your inclination and take the longer path.
examples.cn: 随你的意愿走那条更长的路吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「朝向」与「弯」两部分合起来看：朝一边弯过去，就是倾斜，也是心思的倾向。

root: 拉丁 inclinatio「倾斜」，出自 inclinare「使弯、使倾」＝表「朝向」的前缀＋clinare「弯」；心理义由物理义引申，更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bend: a mind bends toward a choice, a mast bends from upright, the bend is measured, an orbit is tilted, a needle dips, a head bows, a liking forms, ground falls away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「弯」展开：心朝选择弯去、桅杆离开竖直弯去、弯曲被测量、轨道被倾斜、指针下倾、头低下去、爱好形成、地面斜下去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pole pushed at the top, resting at an angle between standing and falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根在顶端被推过的杆，停在一个既非直立也非倒下的斜角上。

branches.en: INWARD LEANING: a mind bending toward a choice and toward a subject are the same bend seen once and repeated.
branches.cn: 向内的弯：心朝某个选择弯去，与朝某门学问弯去，是同一种弯的一次与多次。

branches.en: THE BEND AND ITS SIZE: the leaning of a body and the measured amount of that leaning.
branches.cn: 弯与其量：物体倾过去，以及这个倾斜被量出的数值。

branches.en: SKY AND NEEDLE: an orbit tilted against a plane and a compass needle dipped by the earth.
branches.cn: 天与针：轨道相对平面偏斜，罗盘针被大地吸得下垂。

branches.en: THE BODY'S OWN BEND: a head or waist lowered in greeting is the oldest literal use.
branches.cn: 身体自身的弯：低头或俯身致意，是最古老的字面用法。

branches.en: GROUND THAT LEANS: a slope in land carries the noun back to the physical world.
branches.cn: 会倾的地：地面的坡度把这名词又带回物理世界。

intro.en: Inclination is a Latin noun built from a prefix, a bending verb and a noun suffix, and the same three parts reappear in English relatives, so the word can be read in pieces.
intro.cn: 本词是拉丁名词，由表方向的前缀、表「弯」的动词与名词后缀构成；同样的三部分也出现在英语同族词中，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- supplies direction, clinare supplies the bend, and the noun suffix names the state; the English word adds no further affix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀提供方向，表「弯」的动词提供弯曲义，名词后缀命名状态；英语词本身不再加缀。

items.example: The verb describes a body leaving the upright.
items.exampleCN: 该动词描述物体离开直立状态。

items.example: The prefixed verb added a direction to the bend.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀后，弯曲有了方向。

items.example: The noun named the state of leaning.
items.exampleCN: 该名词命名倾斜这一状态。

items.meaning: a tendency, a tilt or its measure
items.example: The tower's inclination is four degrees.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔的倾斜为四度。

items.example: The path inclines toward the river.
items.exampleCN: 小路向河边倾斜。

items.example: The board is inclined at a low angle.
items.exampleCN: 木板以很小的角度倾斜。

items.example: The committee proved inclinable.
items.exampleCN: 委员会显得容易被说动。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring a slope
items.example: The surveyor used an inclinometer.
items.exampleCN: 测量员用了测斜仪。

items.meaning: the measured tilt of a line or plane
items.example: The inclination angle was recorded hourly.
items.exampleCN: 倾角每小时记录一次。

definition_zh: 倾向于……的；有某种爱好的；倾斜的；有坡度的
definition_en: likely or willing to do something, or resting at an angle rather than upright
core_image: 一块木板斜搭在石阶上，板面顺出一个缓坡；坡上站着的人没往下滑，反而很自然地想沿坡往上走
scene: 晚饭后客厅的话题转到搬家，母亲没有明确表态，只把杯子往儿子那边推了推，意思已经很清楚。The committee was inclined to approve the plan after hearing the cost estimate.
sceneCN: 这里本词指倾向于做某事的（第 1 个义项：心里更可能选择某一边）；句意为听完成本估算后，委员会倾向于批准该方案。

pos.zh: 有某种天赋或爱好的（后接介词）

derivatives.zh: 去掉分词后缀，回到同族动词，语义偏移为「使倾斜；斜坡」
由动词加表状态的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「倾向；倾斜」
由动词加表「可被……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「易被说动的」
由动词词干加表测量仪器的成分构成，语义偏移为「测斜仪」
由动词加表进行的分词后缀构成，语义偏移为「正在倾斜的」

senses.title: Ready to choose one course
senses.definition: likely or willing to do something rather than something else
senses.definitionCN: 更可能或更愿意做某事而非另一事
senses.example: The committee was inclined to approve the plan after hearing the cost estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 听完成本估算后，委员会倾向于批准该方案。
senses.why: The participle turns a leaning into a disposition: the mind has already bent toward one answer.
senses.whyCN: 分词把「倾斜」变成一种性情：心已经朝某一个答案弯过去了。

senses.title: Having a taste for something
senses.definition: naturally interested in a subject or activity and often good at it
senses.definitionCN: 对某学科或活动天性感兴趣，且往往擅长
senses.example: She is musically inclined and plays three instruments.
senses.exampleCN: 她有音乐方面的爱好，会演奏三种乐器。
senses.why: A taste is a mind leaning without pressure, so the same participle covers liking as well as choice.
senses.whyCN: 爱好是不受压力的心思偏向，因此同一分词既能指选择，也能指喜爱。

senses.title: Resting at an angle
senses.definition: positioned at an angle between the horizontal and the vertical
senses.definitionCN: 处在水平与竖直之间的角度上
senses.example: The lamp stood inclined against the wall, throwing light upward.
senses.exampleCN: 台灯斜靠在墙上，把光往上打。
senses.why: This is the literal old sense: a body that has bent away from straight up.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的古老义：物体已经从竖直方向弯开。

senses.title: Built as a slope
senses.definition: having a surface that rises or falls at a steady angle
senses.definitionCN: 表面以稳定角度上升或下降的
senses.example: Goods travelled down an inclined chute to the lower floor.
senses.exampleCN: 货物沿一条斜槽滑到下层。
senses.why: A slope put to work becomes an inclined plane, one of the simple machines.
senses.whyCN: 把斜坡派上用场就成了斜面，即简单机械之一。

senses.title: Leaning one way politically
senses.definition: favouring one party, camp or policy over the others
senses.definitionCN: 在党派、阵营或政策上更偏向某一边
senses.example: The paper is widely thought to be inclined toward the ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸被普遍认为偏向执政党。
senses.why: A mind that leans needs no push, so political sympathy is described with the same participle.
senses.whyCN: 心会自己倾过去，无需推力，因此政治上的同情也用同一分词描述。

senses.title: Likely to suffer from something
senses.definition: more likely than others to develop a particular illness or condition
senses.definitionCN: 比他人更容易出现某种疾病或状况
senses.example: People with that gene are inclined to early hearing loss.
senses.exampleCN: 携带该基因的人易出现早发性听力下降。
senses.why: A body leaning toward a weakness is treated as a statistical tilt, and the participle carries over.
senses.whyCN: 身体朝某种弱点倾去，被当作统计意义上的倾斜，分词就沿用过来。

senses.title: Showing a natural bent for something
senses.definition: showing a natural ability or disposition in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方向上显出天生的能力或倾向
senses.example: He is inclined toward mathematics rather than languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他天生更倾向数学而非语言。
senses.why: The leaning is inborn here, so the participle points to a bent rather than a decision.
senses.whyCN: 这里的倾向是天生带来的，分词指的是天资的偏斜而非决定。

senses.title: Holding a certain opinion
senses.definition: having a view that leans toward one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 持有的看法更靠近某一结论
senses.example: Most economists are inclined to see the slowdown as temporary.
senses.exampleCN: 多数经济学家倾向于认为这次放缓是暂时的。
senses.why: An opinion is a mind at rest at an angle, and the participle describes where it rests.
senses.whyCN: 看法是心停在某个角度上，分词描述的正是它停在哪里。

intro.en: Inclined is the past participle of incline, from Latin inclinare 'to bend towards', itself in- plus clinare 'to bend'.
intro.cn: 本词是同族动词的过去分词，该动词来自拉丁语 inclinare「朝某方向弯」，由表方向的前缀加 clinare「弯」构成。

items.en: Clinare meant 'to bend, to cause to lean', used of bodies rather than of opinions.
items.cn: clinare 意为「弯、使倾」，用于物体，不用于意见。

items.en: Latin in- gave the verb a direction, so inclinare meant 'to bend towards something'.
items.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀为动词指明方向，故意为「朝某物弯过去」。

items.en: English took the verb through French, first for physical leaning and then for leaning of the will.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入该动词，先用于物理倾斜，再用于意志的偏向。

items.en: The participle became an adjective, so a person can be described as bent toward a choice, a taste or an opinion.
items.cn: 分词转为形容词，于是一个人便可被说成朝某个选择、某种爱好或某个看法弯过去。

items.en: Law, medicine and politics use the adjective for likelihood, risk and sympathy, each preserving the image of a tilt.
items.cn: 法律、医学与政治用该形容词表示可能性、风险与同情，各自保留倾斜的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the English verb is recorded from the fourteenth century, while the older base behind clinare is generally considered a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语动词的书记始于十四世纪，而 clinare 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look close and are often mistaken for the participle; group two holds adjectives of willingness and slope.
note.cn: 第一组是与本分词形近、常被误用的形式；第二组是表示意愿与坡度的形容词。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to lean or to make someone willing; the past participle adds the settled result.
entries.definitionCN: 基干动词，意为倾斜或使某人愿意；过去分词则加出「已定」的结果。

entries.definition: The noun naming the leaning or the tendency; the adjective describes a person or thing that leans.
entries.definitionCN: 命名倾斜或倾向的名词；本词描述会倾的人或物。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who can be talked round, built with a suffix of possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 以表可能性的后缀构成，指可以被说动的人。

entries.definition: The present participle describing a leaning under way; the past participle describes a settled angle.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，描述正在发生的倾斜；过去分词描述的则是已定的角度。

entries.definition: Often followed by a verb, it marks a usual direction of behaviour rather than a single willingness.
entries.definitionCN: 常接动词，标出行为的通常走向，而非某一次的意愿。

entries.definition: Stressing consent without resistance; inclined may be only a likelihood, not a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 强调同意而不抗拒；本词可能只是可能性，并非承诺。

entries.definition: Describing a surface that falls away; it says nothing about what anyone wants.
entries.definitionCN: 描述向下倾斜的表面；不涉及任何人的意愿。

entries.definition: Having a weight thrown to one side, usually with disapproval; inclined is milder.
entries.definitionCN: 重量被压向一边，通常带贬义；本词语气较轻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The participle form of a real family: incline, inclined, inclination, inclinable.
normal.cn: 一个真实词族的分词形式：使倾斜、倾向于、倾向、易被说动的。

normal.en: Fixed patterns: be inclined to do, be inclined toward, an inclined plane.
normal.cn: 固定结构：倾向于做、偏向……、斜面。

normal.en: Both a mind and a board can be described by it, which is why the word feels physical and mental at once.
normal.cn: 心和木板都能用它形容，所以这个词同时带着物理与心理两种质地。

normal.en: Everyday phrases such as artistically inclined or mathematically inclined name a taste, not a decision.
normal.cn: 如「有艺术爱好」「有数学天分」这类日常说法命名的是爱好，不是决定。

normal.en: The verb takes a to-infinitive for a choice and a preposition for a taste or an opinion.
normal.cn: 接不定式指选择，接介词指爱好或看法。

abstract.en: Picture a plank laid on stone steps so that a slow slope is made on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板搭在石阶上，有意搭出一道缓坡。

abstract.en: Picture a whole room leaning toward one answer before anyone speaks it aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋子人都朝同一个答案偏着，还没人把它说出声。

abstract.en: Picture a cup pushed a few centimetres across a table as the only reply.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子在桌面上被推出几厘米，就算唯一的回答。

examples.en: I am inclined to think the delay was unavoidable.
examples.cn: 我倾向于认为这次延误无可避免。

examples.en: The road is inclined steeply for the last kilometre.
examples.cn: 最后一段路坡度很陡。

examples.en: She is inclined toward the arts rather than the sciences.
examples.cn: 她更偏向艺术而非科学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「朝向」与「弯」合成的分词：已经朝某种选择弯过去，就是倾向于。

root: 同族动词的过去分词，该动词来自拉丁语 inclinare「朝某方向弯」＝表「朝向」的前缀＋clinare「弯」；更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one participle: a mind bent toward a choice, a taste, a body at an angle, a built slope, a political lean, a bodily risk, an inborn bent and a held opinion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个分词展开：心朝选择弯、朝爱好弯、身体成角、筑成斜坡、政治偏向、身体风险、天生偏向和持有的看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plank laid across stone steps, making a slope that invites walking up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木板搭在石阶上，形成一道引人往上走的坡。

branches.en: THE LEANING MIND: willingness and a settled opinion are the same tilt before and after a decision.
branches.cn: 倾的心：意愿与定见，是决定前后同一种倾斜。

branches.en: TASTE AND GIFT: a liking and an inborn bent both arrive without being chosen.
branches.cn: 爱好与天资：喜爱与天生偏向都不由选择而来。

branches.en: BODY AND GROUND: a thing resting at an angle and a slope built to be used.
branches.cn: 物与地：以角度停着的物体，与被人造出来使用的斜坡。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL LEAN: sympathy for one camp is a leaning the word can name.
branches.cn: 政治的偏：对某一阵营的同情，正是这个词能命名的倾斜。

branches.en: THE BODY'S RISK: a tendency to illness is a statistical tilt of the flesh.
branches.cn: 身体的风险：易患某病是肉体在统计意义上的倾斜。

intro.en: Inclined is a past participle used as an adjective; its base verb is built from a prefix and a bending verb, and those parts recur in the whole family.
intro.cn: 本词是作形容词用的过去分词；其动词由表方向的前缀与表「弯」的动词构成，这些部分贯穿整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- supplies direction, clinare supplies the bend, and the participle ending marks a completed state; English adds nothing further.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀提供方向，表「弯」的动词提供弯曲义，分词词尾标示已完成的状态；英语不再另加成分。

items.example: The verb was used of masts and bodies.
items.exampleCN: 该动词曾用于桅杆与身体。

items.example: The prefixed verb gave the bend a direction.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀后，弯曲有了方向。

items.example: The board is inclined at twelve degrees.
items.exampleCN: 木板倾斜十二度。

items.example: The path inclines toward the mill.
items.exampleCN: 小路向磨坊那边倾斜。

items.example: Her inclination was to wait.
items.exampleCN: 她的倾向是等一等。

items.example: He seemed inclinable to the offer.
items.exampleCN: 他似乎对这提议有点动心。

items.example: The inclining tower draws crowds.
items.exampleCN: 那座正在倾斜的塔引来人群。

items.example: The pilot read the inclinometer.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员读取了测斜仪。

items.meaning: the measured angle of a slope
items.example: The inclination angle stayed constant.
items.exampleCN: 倾角保持不变。

definition_en: the choosing of one thing over another, or the right to be served or paid before others
core_image: 一只盘子里的两块点心本一模一样，拿筷子的人却每次都先夹靠左那一块，动作快得像是早已决定
scene: 早上七点，车站售票窗口前拉起了两列队伍，戴徽章的工作人员把一侧的人先引到柜台前。Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
sceneCN: 这里本词指优先安排或优先照顾（第 2 个义项：把先办、先得的次序给别人）；句意为座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭。

pos.zh: 偏爱；更喜欢的事物（可数或不可数）
